clue.text: Taking on, very taking

definitions.meaning: ... staff or an enemy means taking them on

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: hiring or tackling someone, and being delightfully attractive.

clue.text: Dirty pictures — I'm surprised you initially keep them

indicators.note: keep means the outer letters hold the pictures inside

parts.note: eh is an exclamation of surprise
art means pictures collectively

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of you

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked that you keep smutty photographs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty pictures' looks like one phrase; 'Dirty' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy means soiled with soil, or coarse and bawdy, either of which suits dirty.

clue.text: Section of family includes one outstanding person

indicators.note: includes means the first word holds the second inside

parts.note: in biology a family is divided into genera, so a genus is a section of it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Part of a family contains one remarkable member.
explanation.definitionFit: A genius is a person of exceptional ability, someone who stands out.

clue.text: About four, dashing gentleman is seen to run around

indicators.note: about means the gentleman goes around the number

parts.note: a gallant is a dashing, chivalrous man
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A dashing man is seen chasing around at about four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is seen to' is a link. To gallivant is to go about seeking pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallivant is to roam about in search of fun, a lively synonym for running around.

clue.text: Basic details available from hardware store

definitions.meaning: the practical essentials of a subject
fasteners sold in an ironmonger's, literally

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means fundamental practicalities, and literally names fixings sold in hardware shops.

clue.text: Soldier on show at university

parts.note: to bear marks or signs is to show them
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A soldier is putting on a performance at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier on' looks like a soldier standing on something, but it is the verb phrase meaning to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean to keep going bravely through difficulty, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Female writer's real name; also dame of acting fame

definitions.meaning: Mary Ann ... was the real name of the novelist George Eliot
Dame Edith ... was a celebrated English actress

explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to George Eliot's birth name and to the actress Dame Edith.

clue.text: Fortified drink embarrassed old lady

parts.note: red-faced, so red means embarrassed
a biddy is a slang term for an old woman

explanation.surface: A strong drink left an elderly woman blushing.
explanation.walkthrough: Red biddy is cheap red wine mixed with methylated spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Red biddy names a cheap wine laced with spirit, so a fortified drink in the loose sense.

clue.text: Chap in storeroom is nit-picking

indicators.note: in means the chap is placed inside the storeroom

parts.note: a pantry is a storeroom for food
Ed is a man's name, a typical chap

explanation.surface: A man in the larder is being fussy about details.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive concern with minor details, which is what nit-picking is.

clue.text: Locks ten girls out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of ten girls are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Ten girls are locked out of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' reads as the verb with the girls shut out, but it is a noun: locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Curled locks of hair are tresses of that kind, so locks is a broader synonym.

clue.text: Open tin sufficed

parts.note: a tin is a can
did means sufficed, as in that will do

explanation.surface: An opened tin was enough for the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' poses as a verb applied to the tin; it is the adjective meaning frank.
explanation.definitionFit: An open person is frank and honest, the same quality as being forthright.

clue.text: Without question, help out with calamity

indicators.note: out signals the letters of help and calamity are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: Someone insists, beyond doubt, on helping out in a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something emphatically leaves no doubt, so it is a synonym of unquestionably.

clue.text: Time I met a beautiful woman

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time

explanation.surface: At some hour I had a date with a lovely woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A houri is one of the beautiful maidens of the Islamic paradise; the word is used for any alluring woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a nymph of paradise and by extension any voluptuously lovely woman.

clue.text: Confession producing a charge

definitions.meaning: an acknowledgement of guilt or of a fact
the fee paid to enter, as on a ticket

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: owning up to something, and the price of entry to a venue.

clue.text: Part of motorway is required to receive firmer coating

indicators.note: coating means the firmer word wraps round the other piece like a layer

parts.note: harder means firmer
should expresses obligation, what is required

explanation.surface: A motorway surface needs a tougher top layer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to receive' only joins: HARDER takes in SHOULD. The hard shoulder is the emergency lane at the edge of a British motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: The lane beside a carriageway used for breakdowns is a recognised section of any motorway.

clue.text: Overlooked one at room temperature?

parts.note: un is French for one
something at room temperature has not been iced

explanation.surface: A question of whether something was ignored at room temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as UN NOT ICED: a room-temperature drink is not iced.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unnoticed has gone unseen, the same as being overlooked.

clue.text: Functionary abandoned one of the people turning up

parts.note: an event called off is abandoned
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: laic means of the laity, ordinary people rather than clergy

explanation.surface: An official deserted a member of the public who arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: An official is a person holding a post, a functionary in an organisation.

clue.text: Egghead's clothing put away

definitions.note: read as Egghead is, the definition plus a link

parts.note: a bra is an item of clothing
something put away is in a box

explanation.surface: An intellectual's clothes have been packed up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Egghead's' stands for 'is', so the clue reads as 'Egghead is clothing put away'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainbox is informal for a very clever person, as egghead is.

clue.text: Frog fits into weird winter celebration

indicators.note: weird suggests the letters of frog fits into end up in a strange order

explanation.surface: A frog squeezing into a strange midwinter festivity.
explanation.walkthrough: First-footing is the Scottish Hogmanay custom of being the first visitor across the threshold after midnight on New Year's Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Year visiting custom is a festivity held at the turn of the year, in winter.

clue.text: A coif's badly designed, a disaster

indicators.note: badly designed signals the letters are put together in a wrong order

parts.note: the word coif with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A poorly made hairstyle is a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'coif's' is fodder here, unlike most possessives.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a humiliating failure, a complete disaster.

clue.text: Little food shown in film

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
a pie is a kind of food

explanation.surface: A small meal appears in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: A weepie is a sentimental tear-jerking film.
explanation.definitionFit: A weepie is a tearjerker, a sentimental movie meant to make audiences cry.

clue.text: Crazy about Mum, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: idiotic means crazy or foolish
ma is a word for mum

explanation.surface: Someone is wild about their mother, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like a throwaway aside but is the definition, read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiomatic usage belongs to a particular way of speaking, so the phrase is a literal paraphrase.

clue.text: Cook, perhaps, put on launch

definitions.meaning: ... Cook in New Zealand is an example of a mountain
to stage, as in putting on an exhibition
to begin, as in launching a campaign

explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: a peak such as Aoraki, staging a show, and starting an offensive.

clue.text: Time's opportune? That's nonsense!

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time; the 's means has, joining it to what follows
ripe means ready or opportune, as in the time is ripe

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the claim that now is the right moment as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is slang for rubbish or nonsense, from the cheap offal.

clue.text: I am primarily bound to regret stain

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am

indicators.note: primarily means take only the first letter of bound

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Someone is fated to be sorry about a stain.
explanation.walkthrough: Imbrue is a literary word meaning to stain, especially with blood.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare verb means to soak or stain, typically with blood, so a direct synonym.

clue.text: Scores a century, then bolts

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to bolt a door is to lock up

explanation.surface: A batsman makes a hundred and then runs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolts' suggests running away; it means fastens. A century is a hundred runs in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To clock up points or runs is to accumulate them, an idiomatic synonym for scoring.

clue.text: Non-professionals, receiving the vote, exhibit indifference

indicators.note: receiving means the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: the laity are lay people, those outside a profession
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: Amateurs given a say in matters show they do not care.
explanation.definitionFit: Laxity is slackness or lack of rigour, a careless attitude close to not caring.

clue.text: Group of symptoms —— one my doctor's briefly interpreted

indicators.note: interpreted suggests the letters are reworked into another form

parts.note: Dr is the short form of doctor, with the 's adding S

explanation.surface: A patient has one cluster of complaints quickly diagnosed by the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interpreted' scrambles ONE, MY and DRS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndrome is a set of symptoms that occur together and characterise a condition.
